answer: Each agent registers one reef passage from a ledge and posts a 75-credit bond. A beacon starts the passage clock, bound to one key and one passage serial. Auditors recompute the delta between the beacon clock and the published tide table; a delta over 3 hours, a reused passage log, or a second passage per key burns the bond. First fee 35; the kth passage costs 35+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5030 and 1000 fakes cost 2,532,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented passage fails: a borrowed log repeats the same serial and delta, burning the renter's bond. Honest agents pay 35 once.
